terms.examiner: A Brønsted–Lowry base is a proton acceptor. Be able to pick out the conjugate acid–base pairs in an equation.

terms.definition: An acid that is completely dissociated in aqueous solution.
terms.examiner: A weak acid is only partly dissociated. "Strong" is not the same as "concentrated".
1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶ at 298 K, from the Data Booklet. Its value changes with temperature; pure water is always neutral because [H⁺] = [OH⁻].

terms.definition: Ka = [H⁺][A⁻] ÷ [HA] for a weak acid HA; pKa = −log₁₀Ka.
terms.examiner: For a weak acid alone, Ka = [H⁺]² ÷ [HA], which assumes [H⁺] = [A⁻] and that very little of the acid has dissociated. At half-neutralisation, pH = pKa.

terms.definition: A solution that resists a change in pH when small amounts of acid or alkali are added.
terms.examiner: "Resists change" and "small amounts" are both needed; do not write that the pH stays the same.

terms.definition: The point in a titration at which the acid and the base have reacted in exactly the amounts shown by the equation.
terms.examiner: Choose an indicator that changes colour within the vertical part of the pH curve.
